newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 8.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a decision which has been strongly contested by major investors as it ignores calls from business for a generous, broad-based scheme to replace old infrastructure bonds, next week's Federal Budget will introduce a tightly capped tax rebate system to relace the frozen infrastructure bond scheme, but will restrict rebates to investments in rail and road projects. Page 1.

A packed Victorian Supreme Court heard yesterday former Coles Myer chief executive Brian Quinn was "motivated by greed" when he conspired with Coles' former national maintenance manager Graham Lanyon to conceal A$4.5 million spent in renovations on Quinn' family home. Quinn received a four-year jail term for the fraud, with a minimum term of two-and-a-half years. Page 1.

Australia's main construction union, the Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union, is taking a two-tier approach to the industry's new wages round, setting six per cent a year as a national benchmark for pay rises, which it says is responsive to different economic and industrial conditions in the industry. Page 3.

John Howard added his voice to industry and New South Wales Opposition attacks on the Carr Government's Budget decision to impose a 10 per cent bed tax on central Sydney and North Sydney htels, saying the move was not about tax reform, but about big spending and big taxing initiatives. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following a special meeting with National Party powerbrokers on Tuesday, Prime Minister John Howard has agreed to toughen his 10-point Wik response to ensure all pastoral leases in Queensland and the 5,000 pastoral leases in the western division of New South Wales extinguish native title. Page 1.

Eighteen-year-old New Zealand twins, Joanne and Sarah Ingham, who stowed away on a Malaysian container ship, jumped overboard, spent 40 hours in waters with crocodiles, sharks and deadly stingers then survived for three weeks on an isolated beach, were found and arrested yesterday on immigration charges. Page 1.

Sentencing former Coles Myer boss Brian Quinn to a four year jail term yesterday for his participation in a A$4.46 million fraud, Victorian Supreme Court Justice James Eames said Quinn had been motivated by greed and had fed a "climate of fraud" in Coles Myer to which many had succumbed. Page 1.

Brisbane airport's new owner, backed by the Commonwealth Bank and the Amsterdam airport, Melbourne airport's new owners, which include AMP Investments, Axiom Funds Management and UK airport operator BAA plc, and the investors who bought the Perth airport lan to spend A$510 million during the next 10 years to expand runways as well as domestic and international terminals. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

At least two confused National Party backbenchers called on party Leader and Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer yesterday to explain his last minute decision to accept Prime Minister John Howard's 10-point Wik plan, just one day after vowing to accept nothing short of extinguishment of native title. Howard's plan winds back native title rights, but does not advocate total extinguishment. Page 1.

Releasing the first budget for the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympics (SOCOG) yesterday, Olympics Minister Michael Knight said the New South Wales Government has calculated the cost of staging the Sydney 2000 Games to be at least A$5.2 billion, of which taxpayers will pay about one-third. Page 1.

Former Coles Myer chief Brian Quinn was yesterday sentenced in the Victorian Supreme Court to four years' jail, with Justice Eames ordering that the 61-year-old spend at least 30 months in jail. Eames told Quinn was been motivated by greed and an inflatedopinion of himself when he stole nearly A$4.5 million from the retail giant, and said he showed no remorse for his actions. Page 1.

The Australian Apple and Pear Growers' Association has branded as "a serious breach of international protocol" the actions of a visiting New Zealand scientist who claims to have discovered fire blight on plants in Melbourne's Royal Botanical Gardens. The cientist's comments came after Australian quarantine authorities recently recommended that New Zealand fruit not be allowed into the country amid fears of the disease, often known as horticulture's "foot and mouth disease". Page 3.
THE AGE

Justice Eames in the Victorian Supreme Court yesterday fixed a two-and-a-half year minimum jail sentence for disgraced former Coles Myer chief Brian Quinn, a former Reserve Bank board member and holder of the Order of Australia, for defrauding the retail iant of A$4.46 million. Page 1.

The Federal Government's A$1.307 million sale of the Melbourne airport to a group dominated by life insurance giant AMP and British company BAA was confirmed yesterday along with the details of airport sales in Brisbane and Perth. The Coalition will pocket a total of A$3,337 million from the three sales, with all three airports to be run by foreign operators. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard moved yesterday to reassert authority over the Coalition by demanding support for his controversial 10-point plan to resolve the Wik native title issue. Speaking during a 40-minute press conference, Howard also expressed his imptience with criticism from State leaders. Page 1.

Victorian Ombudsman Barry Perry revealed yesterday his office had ordered an 18-month internal police inquiry into allegations women who have allegedly been sexually harassed were reluctant to talk to police. Perry said two police officers may face criminl proceedings over the allegations of sexual misconduct. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
